Q: How to Schedule Weekly Asyncio Tasks A:

While true loop with asyncio.sleep is not blocking - it async sleeps. It is elegant. It is exactly the same used by nextcord library, just nextcord has additional fallback logic and tries to align the time to full round time https://github.com/nextcord/nextcord/blob/5b06a891a4b4543e65264262e51c62fb0460df06/nextcord/ext/tasks/__init__.py#L151 .

If you want elegant, write your own function decorator for running async a task weekly. Chatgpt is able to generate such decorator in seconds. It will also call asyncio.sleep.

Q: How to get "unique" rows in a Google Sheets QUERY(), ignoring a specific column when factoring uniqueness? A:

Use aggregation in the query statement, like this:

=query(
  'Mileage 2026'!A1:E, 
  "select max(A), B, C, D, max(E) 
   group by B, C, D
   order by max(E) desc 
   limit 10",
  1
)

Note that this will mix row data slightly, as the result will show the latest date and the longest distance that appear with the same B, C, D combo, even if that latest date and longest distance are from different rows in the data.

To avoid that, group by distance as well, use sortn() to only get the first instance of rows where B, C, D are duplicates, and finally use sort() to order by distance descending. You can drop the outer sort if that ordering is not required.

=sort(
  sortn(
    query(
      'Mileage 2026'!A2:E, 
      "select max(A), B, C, D, E
       group by B, C, D, E
       order by E desc
       label max(A) '' ",
      0
    ),
    10, 2, 2, true, 3, true, 4, true
  ),
  5, false
)

See query().

Q: How to Process SQL Query data in Php Codeigniter A:

You want to modify your query to aggregate the marks by category.

Try running:

SELECT 
    q.cat_id,
    SUM(r.marks) AS obtain_marks,
    SUM(q.ques_marks) AS total_marks,
FROM tbl_result as r 
JOIN tbl_question as q on q.id = r.ques_id 
GROUP BY q.cat_id

This should give you an idea how SUM() and GROUP BY works together. Then, just join it up with your other data:

SELECT 
std.reg_id, 
std.name as student_name
FROM tbl_student as std
JOIN
(
    SELECT 
    q.cat_id,
    r.student_id,
    SUM(r.marks) AS obtain_marks,
    SUM(q.ques_marks) AS total_marks,
    FROM tbl_result as r 
    JOIN tbl_question as q on q.id = r.ques_id 
    WHERE r.student_id = std.id
    GROUP BY q.cat_id
) tbl1
ON tbl1.student_id = std.id
